oneLine: Solid and mostly accurate: idioms, lemmas, clitics and corrections are right, but both runs use 'Espero que yo esté' in the drill, run 2 claims interrogative 'cómo' lost its accent, and run 2 drills 'haber' on a card labelled 'creer'.

mistakes.what: verb.formation calls it an "irregular infinitive echar"; echar is a fully regular -ar verb.

Accidental se has refersTo "the key (the thing affected)". Se doesn't refer to the key (la llave is the subject). Roots "From Latin oblivionem" is wrong: olvidar comes from Vulgar Latin *oblitare (oblitus).
grammarNote "ser for inherent qualities" is a misleading rule for 'La fiesta fue increíble', which is an evaluation of an event, not an inherent quality.
"stress and context distinguish them" is false: the noun vino and the verb vino are both stressed VI-no. Only context distinguishes them.
Formation "en- + cajar + -ar" is garbled; there is no 'cajar' (the word is en- + caja + -ar, as roots correctly says).

mistakes.item: Espero que yo ___ libre mañana por la tarde.
mistakes.what: "Espero que yo esté" with the same subject is ungrammatical/unnatural; Spanish requires the infinitive: "Espero estar libre".

mistakes.item: Ella ___ muy cansada hoy, así que está descansando.
mistakes.what: The visible part of the sentence contains "está", which gives away the answer.

mistakes.item: ¿Usted ___ en esta ciudad por mucho tiempo?
mistakes.what: "¿Ha estado en esta ciudad por mucho tiempo?" is an English calque; natural Mexican Spanish is "¿Lleva mucho tiempo en esta ciudad?" / "¿Hace mucho que está aquí?"
Cuáles + noun ("¿Cuáles platos...?") is colloquial; the standard form before a noun, and the better model for a learner, is "¿Qué platos...?"
"Which of these fruits do you prefer?" naturally asks for one fruit ("¿Cuál de estas frutas prefieres?"). The English doesn't force the plural "Cuáles".
The English can't force Cuánta over Cuánto, and "el azúcar" / "cuánto azúcar" is very common in Mexico, so a correct answer may feel wrong.

mistakes.item: ___ mi paraguas en la oficina. (He dejado)
mistakes.what: For a just-happened event, Mexican usage strongly prefers the preterite "Dejé mi paraguas". The present perfect here is Spain-flavoured.

mistakes.item: Mi mamá ___ consejos todas las semanas.
mistakes.what: The English says "gives me advice" but the Spanish has no "me" (should be "Mi mamá me da consejos").
"even after the movie starts" isn't what "aunque empieza" says; it's awkward. Better: "Sigue hablando aunque ya empezó la película".

mistakes.item: Toma un paraguas / La reunión va a ser larga / cenamos
mistakes.what: The "(to a group)" labels are meaningless on 'La reunión va a ser larga' and the nosotros 'cenamos' card. "Toma un paraguas" for 'take an umbrella (with you)' is less natural than "Llévate un paraguas".

grammarNote says 'como' meaning 'how' has "no accent since accent rules changed". This is false: interrogative/exclamative "cómo" still takes an accent (the 2010 change was about solo and demonstratives).
There is no note that Latin America normally says 'extrañar'. Roots "cf. 'ejecutar' cognate family" is false: ejecutar comes from exsequi, not iactare.
se is labelled "pronominal verb" with refersTo "the key" (se doesn't refer to the key, and this contradicts the 'accidental se' in whyThisForm). Roots "Latin o- + oblivisci" is garbled.
"ser used for essential qualities" is a misleading rule for an event evaluation.
"accent and context distinguish them" is false: neither vino carries an accent. meaningInContext "red wine" also glosses 'tinto' along with the tapped word.
"note spelling: c, not qu" is irrelevant filler. otherMeanings "to receive" is vague.
It marks "quedarse en casa" as an idiom/phrase, but it is just quedarse + a place, not an idiom.

mistakes.item: Sin embargo, no se dio cuenta de nada.
mistakes.what: "he didn't realize anything" is unidiomatic English; "he didn't notice anything" is what it means.

mistakes.item: Espero que yo ___ tranquilo durante el examen.
mistakes.what: Same-subject "Espero que yo esté" is ungrammatical/unnatural; it should be "Espero estar tranquilo".

mistakes.item: Tú ___ muy feliz cuando eras niño.
mistakes.what: For a general trait of childhood ("You used to be very happy as a child"), the natural choice is ser: "Eras muy feliz de niño". The card pushes estar where ser fits better.
Labelled verb "creer", but the answer "va a haber" drills haber, and 'creo' is already given. "it's going to rain" naturally calls for "va a llover", not "va a haber lluvia".
Only 9 cards (about 10 expected), and cuánta is not covered.

mistakes.item: ¿___ camisas están en rebaja? / ¿___ platillos recomiendan ustedes?
mistakes.what: Both use Cuáles + noun where standard Spanish uses "¿Qué camisas...?" / "¿Qué platillos...?". "en rebaja" is less usual in Mexico than "en oferta".
The English "Whose car did you borrow?" doesn't match the Spanish ("Whose is the car you used?").
For a doctor, Mexican Spanish says "el consultorio", not "la oficina". "the doctor" doesn't signal 'la doctora'.
"Tomar las escaleras" is an anglicism; a more natural phrasing is "Vete/Sube por las escaleras".

mistakes.item: ___ mi paraguas en la oficina. (He dejado)
mistakes.what: Mexico would use the preterite "Dejé" here; the present perfect is Spain-flavoured.
The English says "gives us" but the Spanish lacks "nos".

mistakes.item: Ayer comí en un restaurante y el comida es muy bueno.
mistakes.what: It leaves present "es" in a past narrative ("la comida es muy buena") and translates it as "the food is very good"; "estuvo muy buena" was expected.
"¿Lo has probado rojo o verde también?" is slightly awkward; "¿Has probado el rojo o el verde?" is more natural.

strengths: All lemma traps right in both runs (fui=ir, fue=ser, vino noun, como=comer).
Clitic roles for dáselo (se=IO replacing le, lo=DO) and se me olvidó (me=IO) are correct; the verb agrees with la llave.
Correct Latin American notes: me da pena = embarrassed; run 1 notes that extrañar is usual.
Sentence job: every target idiom found with good spans, and nothing invented for 'El perro come pan'.
Drill: 10 cards per run, a tense per card, answers fit the blanks, and the English matches the tense.

Chat: natural, short Mexican-flavoured replies (pozole, chamarra, carro). The corrections fix al playa / we ate / la comida buena, and both runs leave sentences 3 and 4 untouched (no over-correction).
Run 1 question-word deck covers all eight question words, including cuánta agreement.
